box: 1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB (sm_120, 188 SMs), CUDA 13.0
note: Single-user, batch 1. plow measured with gemma4_sm120_chat (chunked prefill, no cudagraph); vLLM served TTFT/TPOT from perf-data/vllm_sm120_logs_31b (vLLM 0.25.1, cudagraphs on). plow-fp8 = w8a8 fp8 prefill (PX-2 mma.sync.m16n8k32) + weight-only fp8 decode, bf16 KV. vLLM fp8 = weight fp8 + bf16 KV (KVFP8=0), the fair fp8-vs-fp8 row.

build.emitter: PLOW_UNISEG=1 PLOW_FP8=1 PLOW_W8A8=1 gemma4 <dir> 132096 w8a8.pkt 188 (weights 29.9 GiB fp8)
build.pf_cubin_w8a8: interp_sm120_pf: REG 242, 0 spill (px2 12B was 240; +2 for 31B hd512 flash union)

gates.parity_random_prompt_note: uniform-random ids give an all-near-tie degenerate logit distribution (top-5 within 1.1 logits); bf16=240017 vs w8a8=537 there is the documented 'fp8 disagrees only at bf16 near-ties' budget, not a defect.

w8a8_path_trace_block0.note: QUANT_FP8 exists only under PLOW_NV_W8A8 -> its execution proves the true w8a8 mainloop, not the w8a16 dequant path.

verdict.prefill_vs_vllm_bf16: BEATS at 32k (0.84x); closes 2.1x bf16 gap to 1.12-1.27x at 1k-16k. Not a clean win <32k.
verdict.prefill_vs_vllm_fp8: 1.42-1.76x behind (honest negative): vLLM fp8 prefill is faster.
verdict.decode_vs_vllm_fp8: matches/beats: +2.9%/+1.2% at 1k/4k, -1.4%/-3.0% (faster) at 16k/32k -> the +3-6% fp8 decode gap CLOSED.
verdict.headline: w8a8 fp8 prefill lands on 31B (-36..-42% vs plow bf16), beats vLLM bf16 TTFT at 32k and closes to ~1.1-1.3x below; decode now matches-or-beats vLLM fp8. plow-fp8 does NOT beat vLLM fp8 prefill.

limits: VRAM: a foreign process held 33 GiB throughout. bf16 31B (57 GiB wts + 22.6 GiB KV @ max_ctx=132096) needs ~82 GiB -> did not fit; bf16 parity used a T=2048 packet (small KV). fp8 (55 GiB @ full KV) fit with ~8 GiB headroom. GPU shared under a per-run flock.
